purpose: Montelukast is used to help control asthma and prevent asthma attacks. It is also used to relieve symptoms of seasonal and year-round allergies, like a runny nose, sneezing, and itchy eyes. In some cases, it is used to prevent breathing problems caused by exercise.
how_it_works: Your body releases certain chemicals called leukotrienes when you are exposed to triggers like allergens or cold air. These chemicals cause swelling and tightening in your airways, making it hard to breathe. Montelukast works by blocking these chemicals so your airways stay more open and relaxed.
common_side_effects: Headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, ear pain, sore throat, and runny nose are the most common side effects. Some people, especially children, may have trouble sleeping or feel irritable.
warnings: Important: The FDA has issued a serious warning that montelukast can cause mental and behavioral side effects in some people. These include agitation, aggression, depression, unusual dreams, hallucinations, and even thoughts of self-harm or suicide. Contact your doctor right away if you or your child notice any changes in mood, behavior, or thinking. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Adults and teenagers 15 years and older usually take one 10 mg tablet once a day in the evening. Children 6 to 14 years old typically take one 5 mg chewable tablet once a day. Children 2 to 5 years old usually take one 4 mg chewable tablet or one packet of 4 mg granules once a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
